dialogue_text: Ma'am? Last stop. Chicago. Brett?
My purse... My phone, my wallet, my ID. My mom's ring was in there. The gentleman you were with? He got off the second we pulled in.
He got off the second we pulled in.
Brett! Brett!
Brett! Brett!
Brett! Brett!
Brett! Brett! Ivy. By the time you read this, I'm gone. I married you for your uncle's money. I got what I came for.
I got what I came for. You're a girl from a town with one stoplight. You don't belong in my world. You never did.
Don't look for me. And don't go back to Harlow Ridge. Your uncle doesn't want you there. Neither do I.
Yesterday he said "till death do us part." Is there anybody who can come get you?
I don't know a single person in this city. Then let's get you out of the station first, honey. We'll figure out the rest outside.
Look at this. A bride, all by herself. Where's the groom? What's in the suitcase?
Let go! That's all I've got left! Not for long. Help! Somebody help me!
Hey! Get your hands off that girl's suitcase!
I already called 911. You two want to wait here for the cops? Be my guest. Crazy old lady!
Crazy old lady! Okay. Okay, honey, they're gone. You're safe.
Sweetheart, what happened to you? Where's your family? My husband left me on the train. He took everything I had.
He took everything I had. Well, you've got me now. I'm Maggie. And I'm not leaving you out here alone. My café's right across the street. I'm Ivy.
My café's right across the street. I'm Ivy. Come on, Ivy. Let's get you off your feet.
Eat first. Questions later.
I don't want to be any trouble. I can't pay you. I don't have a dime. Did I ask for a dime? Eat.
Hey, we— Oh, well.
One second, folks. I've only got two hands!
Honey, sit down. You've been through enough today. You helped me. Now let me help you. Thirty years I've been coming here.
Thirty years I've been coming here. Never once seen a bride bus tables. It's been a day of firsts.
Maggie... could I work here? I'll do anything. Dishes, floors.
I'll do anything. Dishes, floors. I learn fast. Work for me? Honey, I've been short a pair of hands since last spring.
Honey, I've been short a pair of hands since last spring. And there's an empty room upstairs. You're not going anywhere tonight. Thank you. I don't even know how to thank you.
Thank you. I don't even know how to thank you. You just did. Look at that counter. It hasn't shined like that in years.
Somebody called about two guys grabbing a suitcase? Two hours ago. Busy Sunday. Sorry.
Two hours ago. Busy Sunday. Sorry. They get away? This girl ran like rabbits. But that's not all. This girl got robbed.
What was taken, ma'am? A white purse. My phone, my driver's license, three hundred dollars cash...
and my mother's gold ring. It's a thin band, with an apple blossom engraved inside. It's the only thing of hers I had. Who took it?
Who took it? My husband. Brett Mercer.
Your husband. Then the DA is probably gonna treat it like a family thing. But— If he sells that ring,
If he sells that ring, that's theft. Every pawnshop in this city has to report what comes through the door. Hang on to that number.
Could I use your phone?
Could I use your phone? I need to call home. Go ahead, honey. Yeah. Uncle Walt, it's me.
Uncle Walt, it's me. Brett left me on the train. He took my purse, my phone, Mom's ring—
That's between you and your husband. You're his wife now. Can I come home? Listen to me, Ivy.
Listen to me, Ivy. Don't come back. Don't you ever come back here.
This one's yours now. Get some rest. I can really stay here? As long as you want.
This house is yours too. I won't let you down. I promise. These were mine, about a hundred years ago.
These were mine, about a hundred years ago. They'll do for now. What are you making?
My mom's apple cinnamon tea. My mom made it every time I got sick. We have an apple orchard back home.
Oh, that's good. Your mama must have loved you.
She did. I miss her every day. I lost a daughter. A long time ago. Then we've got each other now.
Then we've got each other now. You're keeping those? I'd have thrown them in the river.
It's not for him. I'm keeping them so I remember the day I was a fool.
That's three nights now. You haven't slept. I know. I just can't. You skipped dinner too. You can't keep doing this.
You can't keep doing this. Since Dad died, this place has everything in it. Except life.
Where are you going at this hour? A walk. I need some air. Don't drive. Not like this. I'm walking.
Evening. We're about to close. Just a double espresso. As strong as you've got.
As strong as you've got. Espresso? At this hour? Are you planning on sleeping at all tonight?
Sleep's not really my thing. Then you need something else. Like what?
Like what? Apple cinnamon tea. No caffeine. Tea. I asked for coffee.
Trust me. Any sugar in it? Just what the apples bring.
That's... really good. Told ya. Beats another espresso. Keep the change. You earned it.
It's three dollars. Not a hundred. You don't take tips? Not the kind that feel like charity. Five, then.
Not the kind that feel like charity. Five, then. Guess I'll have to come back tomorrow. You can come back.
You can come back. Just don't order espresso at midnight. Goodnight... Ivy.
I'm Adrian, by the way. Who was that smile for?
Just a strange customer. A strange customer who makes you smile like that? I'll take it.
You're smiling. Found a little café by the train station. The café?
The café? Or somebody in it? Let's call it a happy accident.
You're back. No espresso this time. So you came back for the tea. Maybe for the conversation.
Maybe for the conversation. Did you sleep last night? Like a rock. First time in months.
Where did you get the recipe? My mom. She's gone. Five years ago. I still miss her.
Then it's not just a recipe. I know what lonely feels like.
You? You can have a house full of things and nobody to talk to. Well, here you've got tea. And somebody to talk to.
Well, here you've got tea. And somebody to talk to. Is this place yours?
It's Maggie's. When I had nothing, she took me in. Ivy, they overcharged us again!
Supplier bills? Every week. Same order, bigger bill. Look. Same invoice number.
Look. Same invoice number. Forty-four seventy-one. Billed twice. How'd you catch that so fast? I look at numbers all day. You keep the old ones?
You keep the old ones? Every one. I just never knew how to check them. Teach me. I want to be able to do it myself.
Start with the quantities.
Wait. The unit prices are different. Good. And the quantities?
Good. And the quantities? Same. So he's charging us more for every single thing. And we've just been paying it. Remember one thing. People who cheat you are lazy.
People who cheat you are lazy. If a trick works once, they'll use it again. So look for repeats first.
Look for repeats. And before anything else, pull the contract. It's in the drawer with the receipts.
It's in the drawer with the receipts. He delivers tomorrow morning. I'll talk to him. Then I'll be here tomorrow morning too.
Then I'll be here tomorrow morning too. Just save me a cup. Morning. Usual order. Sign here.
Morning. Usual order. Sign here. Hold on, Gary. We need to talk. Some of these bills don't add up. What now?
Invoice forty-four seventy-one. You billed us for it twice. And your prices don't match the contract.
You owe us an explanation. That doesn't prove anything. Everything okay?
He overcharged us, and he won't pay it back. Stay out of it, pal. This is none of your business. If you're cheating these two, it is.
If you're cheating these two, it is. Invoices, contract. It's all in black and white. You can argue with it here, or you can argue with the judge.
Mr. Co— No need for lawyers. I'll pay back the difference. In writing.
I'll pay back the difference. In writing. And from now on, you deliver on the dates in the contract.
you deliver on the dates in the contract. Sure. Absolutely.
Oh! Look at you! Thank you. Really. You didn't have to step in.
You found the proof. I just stood there. Maggie gave me a home. I owe her.
That explains a lot. The way Gary looked at you... like he'd seen a ghost. What do you do, exactly?
What do you do, exactly? I'm... in the hotel business. That explains the numbers. Let's just say I had good teachers.
Let's just say I had good teachers. What about you, Ivy? What do you want?
Someday? A café of my own. Then why not start getting ready now?
Then why not start getting ready now? I could teach you a few things. So now you're a teacher too? Not a teacher. I just know how a business runs.
I just know how a business runs. Okay. But no hard homework. How much bread do you throw out every day?
About a basket. It all goes in the trash. So... that's money too.
You're picking this up faster than I expected. When my mom was alive, I did the books with her every Sunday. For our farm stand.
Last lesson. It's not in any textbook. The harder someone pushes you to sign something,
the more carefully you read it. The morning of my wedding... I signed a whole stack of papers. I didn't read a word.
I didn't read a word. My uncle said they were farm papers. So he could look after the orchard while I was on my honeymoon. What orchard? It's a long story.
What orchard? It's a long story. I've got all night. I never thought I'd end up here. My dad died when I was little.
My dad died when I was little. My mom passed five years ago. She left the orchard to me in a trust. Until I turn twenty-five,
Until I turn twenty-five, my uncle Walt runs it. He always said the place was drowning in debt. That I was just one more mouth to feed. Four months ago,
Four months ago, Brett showed up in town. Said he was scouting land for a client. He was so good to me... I thought he was the one. My uncle gave him money.
My uncle gave him money. Called it a wedding present. After the wedding, my uncle hugged me and said, "Take a nice long honeymoon.
"Take a nice long honeymoon. Don't hurry back." And Brett? He got his money. He didn't need me anymore.
So while I was asleep on the train, he took my things, left me a letter, and walked away. Maggie's the one who saved me.
Maggie's the one who saved me. So what now? I'm not going back to him. I want this marriage over.
You're not alone, Ivy. You've got me. I needed to hear that. Tomorrow, we find you a lawyer.
I can't afford a lawyer. Then we find you a free one. Legal aid.
He wrote it himself. "I married you for the money."
"I married you for the money." "Don't look for me." He walked out the morning after the wedding. We can ask the court to declare the marriage void.
Fraud. Legally, it'll be like it never happened. How long does that take? First he has to be served. He can fight it.
If it goes smoothly, a few months. In Illinois, you've got ninety days from the day you found out you were tricked. You're well within that.
Then I'll wait. What about the papers I signed for my uncle? He's your trustee till you're twenty-five.
He's your trustee till you're twenty-five. He doesn't have to show you a thing. I'll ask anyway. And that police report for your mother's ring? Don't lose it.
Tonight, we forget about all of it. It's beautiful. I've never been down here. What do you miss most? About home.
What do you miss most? About home. Our red barn. My mom painted a white apple blossom on the side. You can see it from the road.
You can see it from the road. With you, I can breathe again. With you, I remember how to laugh.
With you, I remember how to laugh. Do I really matter that much to you? More than you know.
So you're the tea girl. I'll have a cup.
I'll have a cup. I hear somebody comes all the way down here every night for it. Rustic. Where are you from?
Rustic. Where are you from? Michigan. An apple orchard. Michigan land. It's been going cheap lately.
Is there something I can help you with? My nephew has skipped three dinners at the Ashfords'. So I had my driver find out where he goes at night.
So I had my driver find out where he goes at night. Do you know who he is? Adrian Cole. Cole Hotel Group.
Forty hotels. All his. He said he was in the hotel business. Well. He is.
Fifty thousand. Leave Chicago. A man like Adrian marries a woman from his own world.
A man like Adrian marries a woman from his own world. My dignity is not for sale, Ms. Cole.
My dignity is not for sale, Ms. Cole. You can choose where your money goes. You don't get to choose where I stand.
Everyone has a price, dear. Then you've got the wrong guy.
Celeste. That's enough. I'm protecting your future.
I'm protecting your future. My future's mine to decide. Show her some respect. We'll see.
Cole Hotel Group? Ivy—
That's why Gary went white when he saw you. I told you everything about my life. And you let me think you worked at a hotel?
And you let me think you worked at a hotel? I didn't lie. I am in the hotel business. I just... own forty of them.
I wanted you to know me without the money.
The last man who lied to me about who he was left me on a train. I know. I'm sorry.
I need some time to think, Adrian. I understand. I won't push.
Cole Hotel Group's annual gala. Three hundred cups of your apple tea, plus pastries. Ordered two weeks ago. By somebody
Ordered two weeks ago. By somebody named Theo. From Adrian Cole's office. Two weeks ago. Before he ever told me who he was.
Before he ever told me who he was. The deposit's paid. The oven just got fixed, and the property taxes are due next month. Honey, we need this one.
Honey, we need this one. We're going to serve tea. Not to be anybody's date. And the invitation he sent you?
Then at least wear the green dress.
They hired a diner for the gala?
They hired a diner for the gala? It's charming. In a small-town sort of way.
You came. For Maggie's. You should be here. For what you make.
You should be here. For what you make. Babe, you have to meet my dad's partners tonight. Of course. Tonight's a big night for us.
Of course. Tonight's a big night for us.
Well, look who's pouring tea at the Cole gala. Babe, that's the farm girl I told you about. The one who wouldn't leave me alone.
Wouldn't leave you alone? You left me on a train. And this is where you ran to?
And this is where you ran to? What are you doing here? I was about to ask you the same thing. Brett? Who is this?
Brett? Who is this? Go on. Introduce me properly, Brett. I'm your wife.
The one you robbed on a train the morning after our wedding. We're still married. You told me you were single!
Paige, I can explain— He married me for my uncle's money. Then he waited till I fell asleep on the train,
Then he waited till I fell asleep on the train, took my purse, my phone, my mother's ring, and left me a letter. Your uncle promised me a lot more than he paid.
Your uncle promised me a lot more than he paid. So you admit it.
Look around, Ivy. You're pouring tea. You still don't belong in my world.
Oh, I get it. Traded up already? Found yourself a richer one? Talk to her like that one more time.
And who are you supposed to be? I can stand up for myself.
Brett, I have a lawyer. I'm getting this marriage declared void. Your letter is the proof.
And my mother's ring? There's a police report. With your name on it. A husband takes his wife's stuff?
A husband takes his wife's stuff? Cops don't care. You don't get to fool me anymore. Don't call me again.
Stay away from Ivy. Ladies and gentlemen, please direct your attention to the stage.
please direct your attention to the stage. Next spring, Cole will break ground on our very first lakeside resort in Michigan. Cole Harlow Ridge.
That's my mom's barn.
That's my mom's barn. She painted that flower. The seller signed the purchase agreement last week, and we close in ten days. And a special thank-you
and we close in ten days. And a special thank-you to the man who found us this land. Brett Mercer.
You think you won tonight? Your uncle sold your mom's orchard.
Your uncle sold your mom's orchard. And the consent on that contract? That's your signature! You signed it yourself! The morning of our wedding!
The morning of our wedding! Ivy... I didn't know.
Ivy... I didn't know. The whole room heard him. The tea girl is Walt Calloway's niece.
That land you're building on is my mother's orchard. Your mother's trust says the land can't be sold before you turn twenty-five without your written consent.
You gave it. Notarized. Along with a power of attorney, so your uncle could sign for you. Last week he signed the sale as
Last week he signed the sale as trustee, with your consent attached. I thought I was signing farm papers.
Then you should have read them. We're putting this deal on hold. The board already approved it. Walk away from a signed contract with no legal reason,
Walk away from a signed contract with no legal reason, and the seller sues us for millions. Then he sells it to the next developer by Friday.
She's right. You walk away, he sells it to somebody else. And don't you dare pay your way out of this for me.
And don't you dare pay your way out of this for me. If you fix this for me, I become exactly what she thinks I am. Then what do you want?
Every piece of paper my uncle signed with my name on it. I want copies.
It's your consent on that deal. You have every right to see them. You'll have them first thing tomorrow.
Power of attorney and consent. Notarized at ten forty-two
Power of attorney and consent. Notarized at ten forty-two a.m. on your wedding day. In the church office. I was in my wedding dress. He said, "Farm papers.
He said, "Farm papers. Just sign where the tabs are." You can revoke the power of attorney today.
You can revoke the power of attorney today. In writing, delivered to him and to the buyer. After that, he can't sign one more thing in your name.
But the consent you already gave, the contract he already signed? Revoking doesn't touch those.
Revoking doesn't touch those. Not unless we prove he tricked you into signing. Or that as your trustee, he was working against you.
he was working against you. Get me proof he wasn't acting for you. I turn twenty-five in October.
Then he's racing your birthday. The day you turn twenty-five, the land is yours. And so are the books. Brett didn't come to Harlow Ridge to look at land.
Brett didn't come to Harlow Ridge to look at land. He came for me. I'll mail the buyer's copy. Your uncle's...
Your uncle's... you should hand it to him yourself. He'll come. When he's winning, he likes to look you in the eye.
he likes to look you in the eye. Celeste called me. Said my niece was pouring tea
Said my niece was pouring tea at her party in an apron that says "Maggie's." Figured you'd be sleeping under a bridge by now.
Sorry to disappoint you, Uncle Walt. It's a release.
Says you agreed to the sale and you won't make trouble. Sign it, and I'll give you twenty thousand cash.
Sign it, and I'll give you twenty thousand cash. Start over here. Pour coffee for the rest of your life. Why did Brett marry me, Uncle Walt?
Why did Brett marry me, Uncle Walt? 'Cause nobody else was gonna. How much did you pay him? Enough.
You fight me on this, I'll tell everybody in Harlow Ridge you ran off with some city boy
and dumped your mother's debts on your poor uncle. Who do you think they'll believe?
That land was my father's. Your mother had no right leaving it to a girl.
My lawyer said to give you this myself. As of today, you can't sign anything in my name. Go tell the town whatever you want.
Then a judge can hear why. Doesn't matter.
Doesn't matter. Contract's signed. And the closing got moved up. Wednesday, nine a.m. Celeste wants it done before you make a scene.
Celeste wants it done before you make a scene. You don't belong in our world, Ivy. You never did.
Out. Get out of my café. Three days.
Three days. What are you doing here?
Paige dumped me. And your uncle says if the sale doesn't close, I don't get another dime. Ivy, let's start over. We're still married.
We're still married. Half that land money's mine anyway. Come back, we split it, and we're set for life.
That land is what my mother left me. It's got nothing to do with you. My lawyer says an inheritance isn't marital property.
My lawyer says an inheritance isn't marital property.
You left these with me on that train. I kept them so I'd remember the day I was a fool. Take them.
I kept them so I'd remember the day I was a fool. Take them. I don't need them anymore. I'm never coming back to you.
I'm never coming back to you. You think Walt's some honest farmer buried under your mom's debts? He stiffed me too. Ask him where the orchard money went.
Ask him about the casino in Battle Creek.
Everything your uncle gave us to justify the price. Five years of financials.
The trust papers. A draft of the closing statement. It's your consent on that deal. You have a right to see what's behind it.
You have a right to see what's behind it. You didn't have to do this. I'm not fixing anything.
I'm not fixing anything. I'm just handing you the books.
Three years ago. New tractor. Sixty-eight thousand. We've had the same red tractor since I was nine.
had the same red tractor since I was nine. He never replaced it. Picking wages. Harold Bixby, four hundred hours.
Harold died four years ago. I sang at his funeral. Ridge Farm Supply. Invoice eighty-three nineteen...
Ridge Farm Supply. Invoice eighty-three nineteen... Eighty-three nineteen. Same invoice. Booked twice.
People who cheat you are lazy. If a trick works once... ...they'll use it again.
...they'll use it again. The books say we lose thirty thousand a year. Mom's farm stand alone used to clear more than that.
Mom's farm stand alone used to clear more than that. He's been pulling out about two hundred thousand a year. For five years.
"Mortgage payoff, Lakeshore Farm Bank. Nine hundred twelve thousand." He borrowed against the orchard?
And this... "Consulting fee, Larkspur LLC. Three hundred thousand. Paid by seller." The seller is the trust. That's my money. Who's Larkspur?
the trust. That's my money. Who's Larkspur? That's my aunt's house. Your aunt is taking a cut of my mother's land.
Your aunt is taking a cut of my mother's land. And she's the one who pushed my board to approve this deal. She's stealing from both sides.
Wednesday. Let me do the talking. It's your orchard.
That boy showed up in the middle of the night with a binder for you. I know.
I know.
My client is the beneficiary of this trust. She revoked Mr. Calloway's power of attorney on Sunday, in person. The buyer's copy was delivered Monday.
The buyer's copy was delivered Monday. Her consent was signed the day of the wedding and notarized. The purchase agreement was signed before any revocation. It binds her.
Then before anybody signs anything, you should know what you're buying.
A tractor that was never bought. A man who's been dead for four years, paid for four hundred hours of work.
paid for four hundred hours of work. The same invoice, eighty-three nineteen, booked twice. He made my mother's orchard
He made my mother's orchard look like it was losing money so it would sell cheap. And for five years, the difference went into his pocket.
If the seller's side misstated the financials,
that's grounds to terminate. Bookkeeping mistakes. And this. A three-hundred-thousand-dollar consulting fee.
A three-hundred-thousand-dollar consulting fee. Paid out of the seller's money. My money. To Larkspur LLC.
Larkspur Advisory. Fourteen-twenty North Astor Street. Celeste... that's your home address.
It's a perfectly ordinary consulting arrangement— Paid by the seller, out of the seller's money,
Paid by the seller, out of the seller's money, to the executive who pushed my board to approve this deal. This deal is terminated. For cause.
This deal is terminated. For cause. Celeste, clear out your office today. Legal will handle the rest.
You can't sign for me. And you were never my family.
And you were never my family. Stupid girl. You just killed the only thing that could've saved that orchard.
that could've saved that orchard. Two years ago, I borrowed nine hundred grand against it.
I borrowed nine hundred grand against it. The bank's been sending notices since last winter. A week from Friday, ten a.m., the county sheriff auctions it off on the courthouse steps.
the county sheriff auctions it off on the courthouse steps. No deal, no money. You get nothing. Nobody does.
You wanted to come home? Come watch it sell on the courthouse steps.
Let me pay the bank. No. Brett said I traded up to a richer man. If you pay, he's right.
Then let me finish what I should have said that night. I'm sorry.
I hid it because I was scared you'd see me the way everybody does. The money first, then me. You were right to walk away.
No more secrets. I promise. Not one?
Ever since your tea, I sleep about four hours a night. Because I lie awake wondering if it's too soon to go back to the café. That's the last one.
It's not too soon. You want to save it yourself?
Then do what I taught you. If nobody was stealing, what does that orchard make? We picked one point two million
We picked one point two million pounds of apples last year. And who buys apples?
Hotels. Forty of them. I talked to the bank.
The loan's at about nine hundred ten thousand. But you don't have to pay all of it to stop the auction. Just the missed payments since last winter, plus penalties. A hundred and eighty-six thousand.
A hundred and eighty-six thousand. By when? Five p.m. next Thursday. Pay that, the default's cured, the auction's off, and the rest goes back to monthly payments.
and the rest goes back to monthly payments. The trust only needed your consent to sell, not to borrow. That's how he got the loan.
That's how he got the loan. And I've filed an emergency petition in Harlow County to remove your uncle as trustee. The hearing's next Thursday morning.
A hundred and eighty-six thousand. Eight days.
Two thousand four hundred dollars. Frank and I bought this building before you were born.
Frank and I bought this building before you were born. Paid it off years ago. The year Frank passed, I opened a home equity line on it at the bank on the corner.
Just in case. Never touched it. I can draw on it any time.
I can draw on it any time. No. If I lose, you lose everything. I already lost one daughter. I'm not losing another.
You'll always be my daughter, Ivy. Then I'll pay back every cent. With my own apples.
Then I'll pay back every cent. With my own apples. I'm recusing myself. I'm in love with the woman whose orchard this is.
I'm recusing myself. I'm in love with the woman whose orchard this is. That's a conflict of interest. So noted.
These are Calloway Orchard's real numbers for the last five years.
numbers for the last five years. Not my uncle's. Last year, we picked one point two million pounds of apples. His books say we lost money. We didn't lose it.
We didn't lose it. It was stolen. Here's my proposal. Breakfast at all forty Cole hotels.
Breakfast at all forty Cole hotels. Calloway apples, Calloway cider. And this.
This tea. A five-year contract. First year paid up front. Two hundred forty thousand. Why should we trust another Calloway?
Because I'm the one who caught the last one. The land isn't even yours yet. It's on the auction block Friday. Who exactly are we signing with?
Who exactly are we signing with? Then put it in the contract. It takes effect the day the auction's called off and I'm named trustee. If I don't get the orchard back,
If I don't get the orchard back, you don't pay a cent.
All in favor? Approved, with conditions. First year's payment within thirty days of the contract taking effect.
days of the contract taking effect. Ms. Calloway? Chicago PD. Yesterday somebody pawned a gold
Yesterday somebody pawned a gold ring at a shop on Halsted Street. Thin band, apple blossom engraved inside. He showed his driver's license. Brett Mercer.
The first officer told me. If he sold it, it's theft.
I want a deal. I've got something worth a lot more than a ring.
He paid me ten grand to marry her. Promised me forty more after closing. I never saw the forty.
You'd say all that under oath? In a courtroom? If it keeps me out of prison.
You'll get it back when the case closes. Your lawyer asked me to bring him to Michigan Thursday to testify.
to Michigan Thursday to testify. I'll be there. Thank you.
We've got a problem. The bank says the loan belongs to the trust, so only the trustee can pay it. Your uncle called them this afternoon.
Your uncle called them this afternoon. He told them not to take a cent from you. Until the judge removes him Thursday morning,
Until the judge removes him Thursday morning, Maggie's money can't touch that loan. And Ivy? I sent copies of his books
And Ivy? I sent copies of his books to the county prosecutor on Monday. Stealing from a trust is a crime in Michigan.
That niece of mine ran off with some Chicago millionaire. Now she's coming back with a lawyer to take the land right out from under me.
to take the land right out from under me. After everything I did for that girl. Shame. June raised that girl better.
Then I'm going home. We're going home. You okay?
You okay?
Last time, somebody else put me on a train. This time, I bought my own ticket.
Your Honor, the beneficiary abandoned this farm and ran off to Chicago. Now she's blocking the one sale that could have saved it from auction. For five years,
For five years, Mr. Calloway kept that orchard running all by himself. I didn't run off.
I was put on a train. Sixty-eight thousand for a new tractor. The red tractor parked by our barn is the same one I learned to drive on.
the same one I learned to drive on. Harold Bixby, four hundred hours of picking.
Harold passed four years ago. I was at his funeral. So was I. I sang.
So was I. I sang. Invoice eighty-three nineteen, paid twice. Three hundred thousand to Larkspur, a company run by the buyer's own executive.
thousand to Larkspur, a company run by the buyer's own executive. And a letter from Cole Hotel Group, ending the deal because the seller's numbers were false. Bookkeeping errors, Your Honor. She
Bookkeeping errors, Your Honor. She used to make change at a roadside stand. With my mother. Every Sunday. That's how I know what the stand made.
